name: Ralph
own_description: The same model, small enough to run on your phone. Compress the frontier models into GGUFs.

paragraphs: A miner compresses Qwen3-8B into GGUF or safetensors for one of four size tiers while keeping its architecture and weight count. The miner uses a registered Bittensor hotkey, the key a miner works with, to commit a salted hash of the exact files that validators, the participants who score the miners’ work, will fetch from a fixed Hugging Face revision. The miner guide lists no minimum miner hardware or storage, public port, always-on server, paid account or separate judge API key, and the resubmission bond is zero.

Validators run GPU scoring, and three judges compare how the compressed and original models’ next steps change each judge’s predictions about the same continuation. Ralph averages the three scores, using each judge’s weakest result across language and reasoning-depth groups. Binary, ternary, sub2 and sub4 carry weights of 40%, 25%, 20% and 15% across occupied tiers, and those weights are normalized if any tiers are empty. A champion keeps its tier’s full share unless another miner’s best-challenging model earns 20% with a strictly positive paired lower confidence bound. Burn records direct everything to one recipient, and an allocation takes effect on chain when validators apply it.

Each coldkey, the key that holds the funds, gets one entry per tier per round, and losing the saved salt prevents a reveal. The guide says to reveal after the round opens, but the code skips entries whose latest write, including the reveal, has a known block height at or after the block that draws the exam. The lower bound of the 100-block lookback is advisory, and the miner guide gives no fixed round length or registration protection period. Read from https://github.com/RalphLabsAI/ralph at commit 9304344 on 2026-11-23.
mining_note.how_it_was_made: This note was put together by AI agents and not by a person who mines here. One agent read the subnet's public repository and wrote down what a miner does, what it takes and how the work is paid, with a source for each statement, and a second agent opened every source and took out whatever it did not support. Of 23 source checks, 17 held, 2 did not hold and 4 could not be opened, and only what held is in the text above. Nothing of the subnet's code was run, and the note describes the code as it stood on the day and at the commit named in its last sentence, so it can be out of date.
